text.tspan: Turns laws and contracts into machine-checkable rules, and proves on every pull request that the code still obeys them.
Laws change: GDPR, the EU AI Act, HIPAA, Bangladesh Bank rules.
Code changes every day. Compliance is checked by hand,
often months later, after the violation has shipped.
Fines reach 4% of global turnover (GDPR), 7% (EU AI Act).
Legal approves each rule as a plain-language card.
LexCompiler compiles it into formal logic and checks every
code change with the Z3 theorem prover, before merge,
Proof, not opinion: every failure has a counterexample.
Seconds, not months: a pull request check took 5 s;
a rescan after Legal approved a rule took 4 s.
Audit-ready: every decision is signed and hash-chained.
HOW IT WORKS: FROM A NEW LAW TO SIGNED EVIDENCE
it to the rules in force

Step 3 also rescans the main branch at once. A version approved for a later date shows as "Coming up" on pull requests before it fails anything. If a patch can't be proven, nothing is merged: the fix agent only suggests.
ARCHITECTURE: WHAT RUNS WHERE, AND HOW THE PARTS TALK
Runs on your own machine or VPS · code and keys stay inside
tested on a laptop: Windows 11, RTX 4050 6 GB
each agent calls only its own MCP server; what passes between them comes from tool results, never a model
fix pull requests, only after Z3 proves them
publishes the local server to GitHub
proxy headers trusted from loopback only
cloud model through the AI gateway
